newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds mixed ahead of U.S.economic data, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds mixed ahead of U.S.economic data, FOMC.

text.p: Brady bonds were narrowly mixed in extremely light trade on Tuesday as players decided to wait for the release of key U.S. economic reports and the Federal Open Market Committee before making any major moves, traders said.

"Everyone is just sitting back waiting for the (U.S. economic) numbers and the FOMC," said one Brady bond trader at a European investment bank. "We are basically just tracking the U.S. Treasury tick for tick.
U.S. data scheduled for release includes the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) due out today at 1400 GMT and U.S. jobs data on Thursday at 1230 GMT.
The FOMC, the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm, will convene in Washington today and Wednesday, but Brady bond experts said they did not expect a credit tightening.

"People don't expect anything to happen with the FOMC but with the (U.S. Independance Day) holiday on Friday it is speculative to start taking any large positions especially given that you have NAPM today and payrolls on Thursday," said another trader at a European bank.
Although the fundamentals of many emerging market countries continue to improve, market experts said movement in the Brady market is being dominated mostly by the U.S. Treasury market.
Still, traders said Russian dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank loans were 1/4 stronger at 91-3/4 on local buying.
Bulgarian debt also managed to stay in positive territory following the implementation of the currency board system on Tuesday, with its IABs rising 3/8 to 72-1/4 bid.
In the Latin Brady market, Argentine pars were unchanged at 69-3/8 bid, while Mexican pars were 1/8 lower at 77-1/4 bid and Ecuadorean discounts were 5/8 higher at 72-1/8 bid.
